questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The life and prison years of Nelson Mandela
How South Africa's government works today
Important moments in Desmond Tutu's life
The history of the church in South Africa
questions.why: Sam says they're celebrating Tutu's life and will hear about some important moments from it.

questions.q: How was Tutu's role different from some other anti-apartheid leaders?
options: He stayed free and spoke out
He lived abroad for the whole struggle
He was in prison with Nelson Mandela
He believed violence was the only answer
questions.why: Neil says while others were imprisoned or killed, Tutu was there at every step, speaking out.

questions.q: How does Tutu describe his childhood?
options: Lonely, because he had no brothers or sisters
Difficult, because his mother was very strict
Sad, because his family moved very often
Very happy, and his mother treated him specially
questions.why: He says he had a very happy childhood, and his sisters thought their mother spoiled and pampered him.

questions.q: What made the young Desmond Tutu unhappy?
options: His sisters were always angry with him
People took advantage of his kind mother
His mother could not afford to send him to school
His father was often away from home
questions.why: He says part of his unhappiness was that anyone could take advantage of such a gentle, generous person.

questions.q: Why did the Tutu family return to South Africa from London?
options: Because Leah wanted to be near her family
Because they couldn't find work in London
He was made Dean of Johannesburg
Because apartheid had just ended
questions.why: Sam says they returned when Desmond was made Dean of Johannesburg.

questions.q: What happened when Leah went to renew a car licence?
options: She was handcuffed and paraded in the street
She was sent to prison for several years
She was told she could never drive again
She was asked to pay a very large fine at once
questions.why: Tutu says they handcuffed her and paraded her in the streets, though she was later acquitted.

questions.q: Why does Tutu believe the police treated Leah this way?
options: She had broken a serious traffic law
They thought she was someone else
She had refused to answer their questions
To shame her and hurt him too
questions.why: He says they wanted to humiliate her, 'and in the process hit at me'.

questions.q: What did Tutu do at the end of apartheid?
options: He left South Africa to live in London
He started a commission to heal divisions
He took the police officers to court
He became President of South Africa
questions.why: Sam says he forgave the officers and started the Truth and Reconciliation Commission to heal divisions.
